requirement: A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is met.** The implementation matches each clause, and the tests cover the main cases. I judged this from the supplied excerpts and did not run the tests.

**Implementation (`src/lib.rs`, `definition_blocks` and `colon_fence`)**
- **Opening fences.** `colon_fence` counts leading colons, allowing up to 3 spaces of indent. It accepts any line with `length >= 3` and returns the fence length. `definition_blocks` takes that length as `fence_length`, so `::::{req} x` and `:::::::{req} x` are accepted.
- **Shorter colon-only lines stay in the body.** The closer search only accepts a line when `count >= fence_length && suffix.trim().is_empty()`. A `:::` line inside a `::::` block fails that check, so it stays in the body and a nested `:::{note}` directive survives. Lines with fewer than 3 colons are not fences at all.
- **Closers inside code are ignored.** Candidate closers that overlap a CommonMark code block are skipped through `!overlaps_protected(..., &code_ranges)`. The code ranges come from pulldown-cmark `Tag::CodeBlock` events.
- **Closers with at least as many colons end the body.** The first unprotected line with `count >= fence_length` closes the block, so longer closers are accepted.
- **Callers.** The evidence validator (`src/evidence.rs`, around line 234), the book preprocessor, the terms code and the index marker code all use `definition_blocks` or `colon_fence`. They therefore share the same fence logic.

**Tests**
- **`validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers`** (`src/evidence.rs`). It is tagged `{test}` for this requirement. It runs the full validator on `::::`/`::::`, `::::`/`:::::` and `:::::::`/`::::::::`. The body contains a nested `:::{note}…:::` and text after it. The test passes only if the whole body, including that nested directive and the trailing text, is the requirement text and no errors are reported.
- **`colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text`** (`src/evidence.rs`). It is also tagged `{test}` for this requirement. It puts a bare `:::` line inside a fenced code example in the body. That line must not end the body. The body must end only at the real closer, and the text after it must be excluded.
- **`a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive`** (`src/lib.rs`). It is tagged for `requirements.ci.span`, not this requirement, but it directly checks the `::::` opener, the nested `:::` directive and the body bounds.
- **`marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples`** (`src/index.rs`). It covers long fences for the index marker.
- Many other tests use plain three-colon fences.

**Remaining gaps.** There are no FIXMEs. The tests do not exercise every edge, such as a 5-colon opener with a 4-colon inner line or a closing line with trailing text. The code paths for those cases are the same ones the existing tests cover, so I don't count them as gaps.
